# Cyberspace
Every network with a powered router has a region of cyberspace: a pad for each machine on it, paths along its cables, and a gate from the router's pad onto the data bus that joins every network to the city backbone. Pull a machine off the network and its pad and paths are gone; plug it back in and it's where it was.
## Jacking in - Hold a [bold]cyberdeck[/bold] and use it on a networked machine: an [bold]access point[/bold] in the wall, a computer, a router. Beside it, you plug in; up to 8 tiles away and in sight, the deck reaches it through the air. - Your mind goes into your [bold]virtual body[/bold] in cyberspace, on a short spur beside the machine's pad. It looks like you and wears copies of your clothes, but it doesn't breathe, and it bleeds [bold]ghostlight[/bold]. Your real body stays where it is, and can't do anything until you come back. - Use the deck in your hand instead to raise a [bold]practice grid[/bold]: a network of your own, with a training server, that nobody else can reach.
## Your deck Your virtual body is a computer, your deck, with an address on the network you came in through ([mono]ip[/mono] shows it). Its disk keeps its files between runs. Open its terminal from the action bar.
## Jacking out Jack out from the action bar at any time, at no cost. You're thrown out with [bold]dumpshock[/bold], ten seconds before you can jack in again, if: - the deck leaves your hands; - the machine goes off the network, or you lose range of it (2.5 tiles when plugged in) or sight of it (8 tiles through the air); - the path dissolves under you; - your body goes down.
